adams-pearmain.heading: Adams Pearmain
adams-pearmain.flavour: Flesh yellow, crisp, firm, juicy, rich, brisk, subacid, slightly aromatic.

american-mother.heading: Mother
american-mother.flavour: Flesh yellow, tender, juicy, rich, aromatic subacid.
american-mother.quality: Best. One of the best of Apples for the dessert, rather too tender for shipment.
american-mother.note: Season November, February (OCR 'No rember'). Described as 'Mother' (syn. Queen Anne, Gardener's Apple), origin Bolton, Mass.

api.heading: Lady Apple
api.flavour: Flesh white, crisp, tender, and juicy, with a pleasant flavor.
api.storage: may be left on the tree till severe frosts. The Lady Apple is in use from December to May.
api.note: Described under Lady Apple (syn. Api, Api Petit, Pomme d'Api Rouge); 'an old French variety ... nearly always known abroad by the name of Api'. Notes on Api Noir, Api Etoile and Api Gros follow (lines 15998-16019).

emperor-alexander.heading: Alexander
emperor-alexander.flavour: Flesh yellowish-white, crisp, tender, and juicy, with a rather pleasant flavor.
emperor-alexander.note: Heading Alexander, syn. Emperor Alexander, Russian Emperor, Aporta. 'A very large, showy Russian variety.' Same entry recorded for aport.

aport.heading: Alexander
aport.flavour: Flesh yellowish-white, crisp, tender, and juicy, with a rather pleasant flavor.
aport.note: Downing lists 'Aporta' as a synonym of Alexander (Emperor Alexander); same lines as emperor-alexander. Our aport (Aport Alexander) is tied to it only by that synonym.

arbroath-pippin.heading: Oslin
arbroath-pippin.flavour: Flesh yellowish, firm, crisp, juicy, spicy aromatic.
arbroath-pippin.note: Described under Oslin (syn. White Oslin, Arbroath Pippin).

aromatic-russet.heading: Aromatic Russet
aromatic-russet.flavour: Flesh greenish white, firm, brisk, subacid, aromatic.
aromatic-russet.note: An English Apple; description after Lindley.

ashmeads-kernel.heading: Ashmead's Kernel
ashmeads-kernel.flavour: Flesh yellowish, firm, crisp, juicy, aromatic.
ashmeads-kernel.note: A variety from Gloucestershire; description after Lindley.

autumn-pearmain.heading: Autumn Pearmain
autumn-pearmain.flavour: Flesh pale yellow, crisp, firm, a little dry, but rich and high flavored.
autumn-pearmain.note: Downing gives 'Winter Pearmain' as a synonym of his Autumn Pearmain and a long season (October to March); he also has a separate Winter Pearmain entry (line 26011).

baldwin.heading: Baldwin
baldwin.flavour: Flesh yellowish white, crisp, with that agreeable mingling of the saccharine and acid which constitutes a rich, high flavor.
baldwin.quality: Very good. It is unquestionably a first-rate fruit in all respects.
baldwin.storage: Ripe from November to March, but with us is in perfection in January.
baldwin.note: Synonyms Woodpecker, Pecker, Red Baldwin, Steele's Red Winter, Butters printed above the heading. 'In flavor ... belongs to the same family as our Esopus Spitzenberg.'

beauty-of-kent.heading: Beauty of Kent
beauty-of-kent.flavour: Flesh juicy, crisp, tender, with a simple subacid flavor.
beauty-of-kent.quality: Good. A showy English sort for culinary uses.

belle-de-boskoop.heading: Belle de Boskoop
belle-de-boskoop.flavour: flesh a little coarse, crisp, tender, juicy, brisk subacid, rich, and of very good quality
belle-de-boskoop.quality: very good quality; keeps well, and is a promising variety
belle-de-boskoop.storage: keeps well ... Season February to April.
belle-de-boskoop.note: Third Appendix. Trees received from France; Downing says it 'is said to be of Russian origin' (it is Dutch).

ben-davis.heading: Ben Davis
ben-davis.flavour: Flesh white, tender, moderately juicy, pleasant, subacid.
ben-davis.quality: In quality it is not first-rate ... Good to very good.
ben-davis.storage: keeping and carrying well ... December to March
ben-davis.note: Very popular in the Southwest and West for productiveness and late blooming.

bess-pool.heading: Bess Pool
bess-pool.flavour: Flesh white, tender, juicy, vinous, subacid.
bess-pool.note: Origin Warwickshire; syn. Best Pool; description after Hogg.

black-twig.heading: Black Twig
black-twig.flavour: flesh pale yellow, half fine, tender, juicy, mild subacid, rich
black-twig.note: Third Appendix; heading OCR'd as 'Black Tun;'. Supposed origin Lincoln County, Tenn.

blenheim-orange.heading: Blenheim Pippin
blenheim-orange.flavour: flesh white, a little coarse, at first firm, but becoming crisp, tender, juicy, rich, brisk subacid, slightly aromatic
blenheim-orange.climate: This apple is a favorite in England, and succeeds in most localities here in the Middle and Northern States, especially the latter.
blenheim-orange.note: First Appendix gives this 'corrected description' because the main-section entry (lines 7372-7384, 'Flesh yellow, breaking, very sweet, pleasant') was confused with Dutch Mignonne/Blooming Orange.

blue-pearmain.heading: Blue Pearmain
blue-pearmain.flavour: Flesh yellowish, mild, rather rich, aromatic, and very good.

braddick-nonpareil.heading: Braddick's Nonpareil
braddick-nonpareil.note: Originated at Surrey, England; description after Lindley.

calville-blanc-dhiver.heading: White Calville
calville-blanc-dhiver.quality: Hardly good. ... not worthy of cultivation.
calville-blanc-dhiver.note: Heading White Calville, syn. White Winter Calville, Calville Blanche d'Hiver, Weisser Winter Calville. 'A celebrated old French sauce and cooking Apple'. The separate 'Calville Blanc' (line 23627) is a summer Calville.

calville-rouge-dhiver.heading: Red Winter Calville
calville-rouge-dhiver.quality: Poor. An old French variety, quite superseded.
calville-rouge-dhiver.note: Synonyms include Calville Rouge d'Hiver, Calville Royale d'Hiver, Red Calville.

caroline.heading: Caroline
caroline.flavour: Flesh firm, brisk juice, high flavor.
caroline.note: The third of three Downing 'Caroline' entries, the one 'From Norfolk, England' (after Lindley); the other two (lines 8489, 8498) are American.

catshead.heading: Catshead
catshead.flavour: Flesh tender, with a subacid juice.
catshead.quality: Good. ... of little other value except as a cooking apple.
catshead.note: Syn. Round Catshead, Cathead Greening; described as grown in America for drying, no origin given.

claygate-pearmain.heading: Claygate Pearmain
claygate-pearmain.note: Heading OCR'd 'Clatgate Pearmain'. An English Apple.

cockle-pippin.heading: Cockle Pippin
cockle-pippin.note: Syn. Nutmeg Cockle, Nutmeg Pippin, White Cockle, Brown Cockle; from Sussex.

colonel-vaughan.heading: Kentish Pippin
colonel-vaughan.flavour: Flesh yellowish white, crisp, tender, juicy, rich, brisk subacid.
colonel-vaughan.quality: Good. An old English Apple esteemed abroad for cooking, but is here quite good for dessert.
colonel-vaughan.storage: December to May. Valuable as a late keeper.
colonel-vaughan.note: Kentish Pippin with syn. Red Kentish Pippin, Vaun's Pippin - names in our aka; but Downing's fruit is greenish yellow with a slight blush, a late keeper. A separate 'Vaughn's Pippin' (syn. Colonel Vaughn's, line 24829, waxen yellow with crimson, sweet, Sept-Oct, after Hogg) may be the intended apple; homonym doubt.

cornish-aromatic.heading: Cornish Aromatic
cornish-aromatic.flavour: Flesh yellow, with a rich, aromatic, subacid flavor.

cornish-gilliflower.heading: Cornish Gilliflower
cornish-gilliflower.flavour: Flesh yellowish, firm, with a rich, high flavor, and a slight aromatic perfume.
cornish-gilliflower.note: Tree 'a poor grower and shy bearer'.

costard.heading: Costard
costard.flavour: Flesh greenish white, tender, juicy, brisk, subacid.
costard.note: Syn. Coulthard, Prussian Pippin; description after Hogg.

court-pendu-plat.heading: Court Pendu Plat
court-pendu-plat.flavour: Flesh yellow, crisp, with a rich brisk acid flavor.
court-pendu-plat.note: Many synonyms incl. Court-pendu Musque, Garnon's Apple, Wollaton Pippin. 'A popular French variety.'

coxs-orange-pippin.heading: Cox's Orange Pippin
coxs-orange-pippin.flavour: Flesh yellowish, rather firm, juicy, brisk, rich, subacid.
coxs-orange-pippin.quality: Very Good. An English variety much esteemed for dessert.

coxs-pomona.heading: Cox's Pomona
coxs-pomona.flavour: Flesh white, crisp, juicy, brisk subacid.
coxs-pomona.quality: Good. ... valuable as a culinary apple.

darcy-spice.heading: Baddow Pippin
darcy-spice.flavour: Flesh whitish, firm, crisp, rich vinous.
darcy-spice.quality: Good. An English dessert Apple, valued for its keeping properties.
darcy-spice.storage: valued for its keeping properties ... April to May.
darcy-spice.note: Described as Baddow Pippin, syn. 'Ribston Pippin, Spring' (our aka Baddow Pippin, Spring Ribston). No mention of spice.

devonshire-quarrenden.heading: Devonshire Quarrenden
devonshire-quarrenden.flavour: Flesh nearly white, crisp, juicy, with a pleasant subacid flavor.
devonshire-quarrenden.storage: Ripe during all August and September.

duchess-of-oldenburg.heading: Duchess of Oldenburgh
duchess-of-oldenburg.flavour: The flesh is juicy, sprightly subacid.
duchess-of-oldenburg.quality: although not of the first quality, always commands a ready sale, as it is valuable for market and cooking, and passably good for dessert.
duchess-of-oldenburg.climate: This handsome Russian Apple proves one of the most hardy and profitable varieties in cultivation, and especially in our northwestern sections.

duke-of-devonshire.heading: Duke of Devonshire
duke-of-devonshire.flavour: Flesh yellowish, crisp, juicy, rich, sugary, fine aroma.
duke-of-devonshire.note: Heading OCR'd 'Duke of Devonshibe'; description after Hogg.

early-harvest.heading: Early Harvest
early-harvest.flavour: Flesh very white, tender, and juicy, crisp, with a rich sprightly subacid flavor.
early-harvest.quality: Very good to best. ... we think it the finest early apple yet known.
early-harvest.storage: It begins to ripen about the first of July, and continues in use all that month.
early-harvest.note: Syn. Prince's Harvest, July Pippin, Tart Bough, Yellow Harvest, Large White Juneating.

esopus-spitzenburg.heading: Esopus Spitzenburgh
esopus-spitzenburg.flavour: Flesh yellow, rather firm, crisp, juicy, with a delicious rich, brisk flavor.
esopus-spitzenburg.quality: Best. ... a handsome, truly delicious Apple ... unsurpassed as a dessert fruit by any other variety.
esopus-spitzenburg.note: Throughout New York 'considered the first of apples'.

fall-pippin.heading: Fall Pippin
fall-pippin.flavour: Flesh white, very tender and mellow, with a rich, aromatic flavor.
fall-pippin.quality: Very good to best. The Fall Pippin is a noble fruit, and is considered the first of autumn apples in the Middle States
fall-pippin.note: Syn. York Pippin, Philadelphia Pippin, Pound Pippin.

flower-of-kent.heading: Flower of Kent
flower-of-kent.flavour: Flesh greenish yellow, abounding with a lively subacid juice.
flower-of-kent.note: 'Chiefly valued for baking and kitchen use.'

golden-knob.heading: Golden Knob
golden-knob.flavour: Flesh greenish white, crisp, juicy, brisk, sweet.
golden-knob.note: Short entry with no origin given; small golden russeted fruit fits the English Golden Knob.

golden-noble.heading: Golden Noble
golden-noble.quality: An old English variety, valuable for cooking.

golden-russet.heading: Golden Russet
golden-russet.flavour: Flesh whitish yellow, fine-grained, rather compact, sprightly, mild subacid.
golden-russet.climate: It is one of the popular Apples, succeeding in nearly all sections, and especially in rich Western soils.
golden-russet.note: Syn. English Golden Russet; Downing treats it as the old English apple of Ronalds and Lindley widely grown in America. A different 'Golden Russet, of Massachusetts' follows (line 13226), and the American Golden Russet (line 6073) is another apple; 'many Golden Russets about the country'.

gravenstein.heading: Gravenstein
gravenstein.flavour: Flesh tender and crisp, with a high-flavored, somewhat aromatic taste.
gravenstein.quality: Very good. ... unquestionably, a fruit of first-rate quality.
gravenstein.climate: A valuable apple for market or cooking, succeeding admirably wherever grown.

grimes-golden.heading: Grimes' Golden Pippin
grimes-golden.flavour: Flesh yellow, compact, crisp, tender, juicy, rich, sprightly, spicy subacid, peculiar aroma.
grimes-golden.climate: In its native locality it is highly prized for the peculiar hardihood of the tree, withstanding uninjured the most severe winters

hagloe-crab.heading: Hagloe Crab
hagloe-crab.quality: a celebrated old English cider fruit.
hagloe-crab.note: Describes only the fruit's shape and skin.

hambledon-deux-ans.heading: Hambledon Deux Ans
hambledon-deux-ans.note: Origin Hampshire. The season given (November) is far shorter than the name implies.

hawthornden.heading: Hawthornden
hawthornden.flavour: Flesh white, juicy, of a simple, pleasant flavor.
hawthornden.quality: Good. ... inferior to that fruit [Maiden's Blush] in flavor.
hawthornden.note: Syn. White Hawthornden. A New or winter Hawthornden, 'a longer keeper', is noted at the end.

hereford-redstreak.heading: Red Streak
hereford-redstreak.flavour: Flesh yellow, rich, firm, and dry.
hereford-redstreak.quality: Good. A capital English cider Apple ... it makes a rich, high flavored, strong liquor.
hereford-redstreak.climate: which thrives admirably in this country
hereford-redstreak.note: Syn. Herefordshire Red Streak, Scudamore's Crab.

hewes-crab.heading: Hewe's Virginia Crab
hewes-crab.flavour: Flesh fibrous, with an acid, rough, and astringent flavor
hewes-crab.quality: The Virginia Crab makes a very high-flavored dry cider, which, by connoisseurs, is thought unsurpassed in flavor by any other
hewes-crab.storage: retains its soundness a long time.
hewes-crab.note: Storage remark refers to the cider. Roane's White Crab noted as a sub-variety.

hubbardston-nonesuch.heading: Hubbardston Nonsuch
hubbardston-nonesuch.flavour: Flesh yellow, juicy, and tender, with an agreeable mingling of sweetness and acidity in its flavor.
hubbardston-nonesuch.quality: Very good to best. ... It is worthy of extensive orchard culture.
hubbardston-nonesuch.note: Syn. John May, Old Town Pippin.

irish-peach.heading: Irish Peach Apple
irish-peach.flavour: Flesh white, tender, juicy, and pretty well flavored.

jonathan.heading: Jonathan
jonathan.flavour: Flesh white, rarely a little pinkish, very tender and juicy, with a mild, sprightly, vinous flavor.
jonathan.quality: Best. ... a very beautiful dessert Apple ... one of the best in quality, and most profitable either for table or market.
jonathan.note: The heading line is lost in the OCR; the entry starts with the synonyms King Philip, Philip Rick. 'This fruit evidently belongs to the Spitzenburgh class.'

kentish-fillbasket.heading: Kentish Fill-Basket
kentish-fillbasket.flavour: Flesh tender, juicy, with a subacid, sprightly flavor.
kentish-fillbasket.quality: Good. The flavor is tolerable, and it is an excellent cooking Apple.
kentish-fillbasket.note: Syn. Potter's Large Seedling, Lady de Grey's.

kerry-pippin.heading: Kerry Pippin
kerry-pippin.flavour: Flesh yellow, tender, crisp, with a sugary flavor.

keswick-codlin.heading: Keswick Codlin
keswick-codlin.flavour: Flesh yellowish white, juicy, with a pleasant acid flavor.
keswick-codlin.quality: A noted English cooking Apple ... one of the most profitable of orchard sorts for cooking or market.
keswick-codlin.storage: may be gathered for tarts as early as the month of August, and continues in use till November.

king-of-the-pippins.heading: King of the Pippins
king-of-the-pippins.quality: An English fruit of poor quality ... Good.
king-of-the-pippins.note: Syn. Hampshire Yellow. The OCR places a 'King of Tompkins County' caption line just above (15738).

tompkins-king.heading: King of Tompkins County
tompkins-king.flavour: Flesh yellowish, rather coarse, juicy, tender, with an exceedingly agreeable, rich, vinous flavor, delightfully aromatic.
tompkins-king.quality: Very good to best. A valuable market fruit.
tompkins-king.note: Syn. King Apple, Toms Red, Tommy Red.

kingston-black.heading: Kingston Black
kingston-black.flavour: Flesh white, stained with red, tender, juicy, sweet.
kingston-black.quality: A small English cider fruit of little value.
kingston-black.note: Downing's fruit is 'pale yellow, striped with red' and 'sweet', unlike the dark-red bittersharp Kingston Black; possibly a misdescription or another apple of the name.

knobby-russet.heading: Knobby Russet
knobby-russet.flavour: Flesh yellowish, crisp, not juicy, but sweet and high flavored.
knobby-russet.quality: A dessert Apple from Sussex, England
knobby-russet.note: Syn. Knobbed Russet, Old Maid's, Winter Russet; after Lindley.

lady-henniker.heading: Lady Henniker
lady-henniker.flavour: flesh very tender in the grain, well flavored, and with a pleasant perfume.
lady-henniker.quality: chiefly valuable as a cooking variety, but useful also in the dessert.
lady-henniker.note: Second Appendix; from the Journal of Horticulture.

lady-of-wemyss.heading: Lady of the Wemyss
lady-of-wemyss.quality: A large and handsome Scotch Apple.

landsberger-reinette.heading: Landsberger Reinette
landsberger-reinette.flavour: flesh yellowish, fine, crisp, tender, juicy, lively subacid, rather rich
landsberger-reinette.note: First Appendix; heading garbled in OCR, syn. Reinette de Landsberg.

leathercoat-russet.heading: Royal Russet
leathercoat-russet.flavour: Flesh greenish white, firm, rich acid.
leathercoat-russet.note: Royal Russet, syn. Leathercoat Russet, Reinette de Canada Grise. A separate 'Old Royal Russet' (syn. Leather Coat Russet, line 18854, 'sharp subacid', after Elliott) also exists.

limbertwig.heading: Limber Twig
limbertwig.flavour: Flesh whitish, not very tender, juicy, with a brisk, subacid flavor.
limbertwig.note: Syn. James River; much cultivated South and West, supposed origin North Carolina.

lodgemore-nonpareil.heading: Lodgemore Nonpareil
lodgemore-nonpareil.flavour: Flesh yellowish, firm, crisp, juicy, aromatic.

london-pippin.heading: London Pippin
london-pippin.quality: Good. A very old English Apple, mostly valued for cooking or drying
london-pippin.note: Syn. Five-Crowned Pippin, Royal Somerset; a separate short 'Royal Somerset' entry (line 21864, after Hogg) also exists.

lord-suffield.heading: Lord Suffield
lord-suffield.flavour: Flesh white, firm, tender, brisk subacid.
lord-suffield.quality: A valuable English kitchen Apple, described as an improvement on Keswick Codlin.

magnum-bonum.heading: Bonum
magnum-bonum.flavour: Flesh white, often stained next the skin, firm, tender, juicy, rich, mild subacid.
magnum-bonum.note: Bonum, syn. Magnum Bonum; raised in Davidson Co., N. C.

manks-codlin.heading: Mank's Codlin
manks-codlin.flavour: Flesh yellowish white, fine crisp, brisk subacid.
manks-codlin.quality: Good. An old English culinary Apple
manks-codlin.note: Syn. Irish Pitcher, Irish Codlin, Eve of Scotland, Frith Pippin.

margil.heading: Margil
margil.quality: Good. An old English dessert Apple

mcintosh-red.heading: McIntosh Red
mcintosh-red.flavour: flesh white, fine, very tender, juicy, mild subacid, refreshing, peculiar slight quince-like flavor
mcintosh-red.quality: a good annual bearer of fair, handsome fruit of excellent quality
mcintosh-red.climate: the tree is said to be very hardy, long-lived, vigorous

mere-de-menage.heading: Mere de Menage
mere-de-menage.flavour: Flesh firm, crisp, brisk, juicy, subacid.
mere-de-menage.quality: A very showy market Apple, and good for cooking.

newtown-pippin.heading: Green Newtown Pippin
newtown-pippin.flavour: Flesh greenish white, very juicy, crisp, with a fine aroma, and an exceedingly high and delicious flavor.
newtown-pippin.quality: Best. The Newtown Pippin stands at the head of all Apples
newtown-pippin.storage: This is one of the finest keeping apples, and is in eating from December to May, but is in the finest perfection in March.
newtown-pippin.climate: it requires a pretty strong, deep, warm soil to attain its full perfection, and in the orchard it should be well manured every two or three years.
newtown-pippin.note: Syn. Newtown Pippin, American Newtown Pippin. The Yellow Newtown Pippin (syn. Albemarle Pippin, lines 26337-26353) is described separately as having 'a higher perfume' and being 'more highly fragrant'.

nonpareil.heading: Nonpareil
nonpareil.flavour: Flesh crisp, juicy, vinous, aromatic, mild acid.
nonpareil.note: Syn. English Nonpareil, Old Nonpareil, Reinette Nonpareil.

norfolk-beefing.heading: Norfolk Beaufin
norfolk-beefing.quality: Good. A large English fruit, only fit for cooking purposes
norfolk-beefing.note: Syn. Read's Baker, Catshead Beaufin, Norfolk Beefing.

northern-spy.heading: Northern Spy
northern-spy.flavour: one of the most delicious, fragrant, and sprightly of all late dessert apples. Flesh white, fine-grained, tender, slightly subacid, with a peculiarly fresh and delicious flavor.
northern-spy.storage: It ripens in January, keeps till June
northern-spy.climate: The trees require high culture, and open heads to let in the sun, otherwise the fruit is wanting in flavor, and apt to be imperfect and knotty.

orleans-reinette.heading: Orleans Reinette
orleans-reinette.flavour: Flesh yellowish, fine, juicy, brisk acid.
orleans-reinette.note: Syn. Reinette d'Orleans. Very short entry.

peasgoods-nonsuch.heading: Peasgood's Nonesuch
peasgoods-nonsuch.flavour: flesh yellowish, tender, very juicy, with an agreeable acid flavor.
peasgoods-nonsuch.quality: a fine culinary or dessert apple

pecks-pleasant.heading: Peck's Pleasant
pecks-pleasant.flavour: Flesh yellowish, fine-grained, juicy, crisp and tender, with a delicious, high aromatic sprightly subacid.
pecks-pleasant.quality: Very good or best. A first-rate fruit in all respects
pecks-pleasant.note: Syn. Waltz Apple; 'belonging to the Newtown Pippin class'.

pitmaston-pine-apple.heading: Pitmaston Pine-Apple
pitmaston-pine-apple.note: After Hogg; no pine-apple flavour mentioned.

pomme-gris.heading: Pomme Grise
pomme-gris.quality: Very good to best. ... undoubtedly one of the finest dessert Apples for a northern climate.
pomme-gris.climate: one of the finest dessert Apples for a northern climate.
pomme-gris.note: A small gray Apple from Canada; syn. Gray Apple.

ralls-janet.heading: Rawle's Janet
ralls-janet.flavour: Flesh whitish yellow, tender, juicy, pleasant subacid.
ralls-janet.climate: it puts forth its leaves and blossoms much later than other varieties in the spring, and consequently avoids injury by late frost; it is, therefore, particularly valuable for the South and Southwest ... So far has not succeeded well at the North.
ralls-janet.note: Syn. Neverfail, Jennett, Rock Rimmon and others.

red-astrachan.heading: Red Astrachan
red-astrachan.flavour: Flesh quite white, crisp, moderately juicy, with an agreeable, rich, acid flavor.
red-astrachan.quality: Good to very good. It is one of the handsomest dessert fruits, and its quality is good
red-astrachan.storage: if not taken from the tree as soon as ripe it is liable to become mealy. ... Ripens from last of July to middle of August.

rhode-island-greening.heading: Rhode Island Greening
rhode-island-greening.flavour: Flesh yellow, fine-grained, tender, crisp, with an abundance of rich, slightly aromatic, lively, acid juice.
rhode-island-greening.quality: Very good. ... one of the most esteemed and profitable among early winter fruits.
rhode-island-greening.climate: It succeeds well in almost all of the northern sections of the States, and on a great variety of soils ... In Southern Ohio, Indiana, and farther south it drops too early.

ribston-pippin.heading: Ribston Pippin
ribston-pippin.flavour: Flesh deep yellow, firm, crisp, with a sharp, rich, aromatic flavor.
ribston-pippin.quality: Very good. ... to say that an Apple has a Ribston flavor is there the highest praise that can be bestowed.
ribston-pippin.climate: But it is scarcely so much esteemed here ... In Maine, and parts of Canada, it is very fine and productive.
ribston-pippin.note: Syn. Glory of York, Formosa Pippin.

rome-beauty.heading: Rome Beauty
rome-beauty.flavour: Flesh yellowish, tender, juicy, sprightly subacid.
rome-beauty.note: Syn. Gillett's Seedling; origin Southern Ohio.

rosemary-russet.heading: Rosemary
rosemary-russet.flavour: Flesh firm, yellowish, rich, and good for table or kitchen use.
rosemary-russet.quality: good for table or kitchen use.
rosemary-russet.note: Heading Rosemary, syn. Rosemary Russet; after Ronalds.

ross-nonpareil.heading: Ross Nonpareil
ross-nonpareil.flavour: Flesh greenish white, tender, with a rich aromatic flavor.
ross-nonpareil.storage: Very subject to rot before ripening. ... October.
ross-nonpareil.note: An Irish fruit. No mention of fennel or anise.

roxbury-russet.heading: Roxbury Russet
roxbury-russet.flavour: Flesh greenish white, moderately juicy, with a rather rich subacid flavor.
roxbury-russet.storage: keeps till late in the spring wherever the soil and climate suit it. ... Ripens in January, and may be brought to market in June.
roxbury-russet.climate: South and West it drops its fruit too early, and is therefore not valuable.
roxbury-russet.note: Syn. Boston Russet, Putnam Russet, Sylvan Russet and others.

sam-young.heading: Sam Young
sam-young.flavour: Flesh greenish, quite juicy and tender.

sheepnose.heading: Black Gilliflower
sheepnose.quality: Good. ... some call it a profitable market fruit.
sheepnose.note: Black Gilliflower is in our aka; Downing's own 'Sheepnose' entry (line 22376) says the name covers several apples and gives two other descriptions.

smokehouse.heading: Smokehouse
smokehouse.flavour: Flesh yellowish, somewhat firm, juicy, crisp, rather rich subacid.
smokehouse.note: Syn. Millcreek Vandevere, Red Vandevere, English Vandevere (OCR prints Millcreek Vandevere first).

sops-in-wine.heading: Sops of Wine
sops-in-wine.flavour: Flesh white, often stained, not very juicy, mild, pleasant subacid.
sops-in-wine.note: An old European variety; many American synonyms.

stayman-winesap.heading: Stayman's Winesap
stayman-winesap.flavour: flesh yellow, firm, tender, juicy, rich, mild subacid, aromatic
stayman-winesap.storage: fruit hangs well on the tree. ... Season January to May.
stayman-winesap.note: Third Appendix; quoting Dr. Stayman's own description.

summer-rambo.heading: Summer Rambo
summer-rambo.quality: Good. ... the old trees of which everywhere prove hardy and profitable for early marketing.
summer-rambo.note: Syn. Rambour Franc, Summer Rambour, Rambour d'Ete; 'an old French Apple'.

swaar.heading: Swaar
swaar.flavour: Flesh yellowish, fine-grained, tender, with an exceedingly rich aromatic flavor and a spicy smell.
swaar.quality: Very good to best. ... It is one of the finest flavored apples in America
swaar.storage: the fruit is in season from December to March.
swaar.climate: It requires a deep, rich, sandy loam to bring it to perfection ... though it does not succeed well in damp or cold soils.

tolman-sweet.heading: Talman's Sweet
tolman-sweet.flavour: Flesh quite white, rather firm, fine-grained, with a rich sweet flavor.
tolman-sweet.quality: In quality the fruit is scarcely second rate as a table sort, but it is a very popular and profitable orchard sort
tolman-sweet.note: Syn. Tolman's Sweeting, Tallman's Sweeting; valued for 'the hardihood of the trees' and for stock feeding.

tom-putt.heading: Tom Potter
tom-putt.note: 'A Devonshire, England, Apple, described by Ronalds', yellow striped red, Sept-Oct; 'Tom Potter' is probably a corruption of Tom Putt, but not certain.

tower-of-glamis.heading: Tower of Glammis
tower-of-glamis.flavour: Flesh white, tender, juicy, sharp subacid.
tower-of-glamis.quality: Good. A fine culinary Apple from the Clydesdale orchards, Scotland.
tower-of-glamis.note: Syn. Glammis Castle, Carse of Gowrie.

twenty-ounce.heading: Twenty Ounce
twenty-ounce.quality: Good to very good. It is a good, sprightly fruit, though not very high flavored
twenty-ounce.note: Syn. Morgan's Favorite, Cayuga Red Streak, Wine of Connecticut and others.

warners-king.heading: Warner's King
warners-king.flavour: Flesh white, tender, crisp, brisk subacid.

wealthy.heading: Wealthy
wealthy.flavour: Flesh white, fine-grained, stained with red, tender, juicy, lively, vinous, subacid.
wealthy.climate: So far the tree has proved hardy, vigorous, and healthy.
wealthy.note: Raised by Peter M. Gideon near St. Paul, Minn.; repeated in the First Appendix (line 90699).

westfield-seek-no-further.heading: Westfield Seek-no-Further
westfield-seek-no-further.flavour: Flesh white, fine-grained, tender, with a rich pearmain flavor.
westfield-seek-no-further.quality: Very good or best. A first-rate fruit

wheelers-russet.heading: Wheeler's Russet
wheelers-russet.flavour: Flesh firm, greenish white, brisk, saccharine.
wheelers-russet.note: Originated in Gloucester, England; after Lindley.

white-transparent.heading: Yellow Transparent
white-transparent.flavour: flesh white, half fine, tender, juicy, sprightly subacid
white-transparent.storage: does not continue long in use ... Season early in August, and a week or two before Tetofsky.
white-transparent.climate: promises to be valuable for a cold climate as an early fruit of good quality
white-transparent.note: Third Appendix; 'a new Russian variety ... imported from St. Petersburg in 1870'. Yellow Transparent is the American name of White Transparent.

winesap.heading: Winesap
winesap.flavour: Flesh yellow, firm, crisp, with a rich, high flavor.
winesap.quality: Very good. This is not only a good Apple for the table, but it is also one of the very finest cider fruits
winesap.storage: the apples have the good quality of hanging late upon the trees without injury ... November to May.
winesap.climate: the tree thrives well on sandy, light soils. The tree is very hardy

winter-pearmain.heading: Winter Pearmain
winter-pearmain.flavour: Flesh yellowish, firm, crisp, juicy, slightly aromatic.
winter-pearmain.quality: This is one of the oldest Apples on record.
winter-pearmain.note: Syn. Old Pearmain, Great Pearmain, Pearmain d'Hiver; none of our aka appear. Two unrelated American 'Winter Pearmains' follow (lines 26030-26045), and Downing's Autumn Pearmain also lists Winter Pearmain as a synonym.

wolf-river.heading: Wolf River
wolf-river.flavour: flesh white, rather coarse, half tender, juicy, pleasant, mild subacid, with a peculiar spicy, slight quince-like flavor
wolf-river.quality: rather better in quality [than the Alexander]
wolf-river.climate: The tree is said to be very hardy
wolf-river.note: Third Appendix; supposed seedling of the Alexander.

wyken-pippin.heading: Wyken Pippin
wyken-pippin.flavour: Flesh yellowish, tender, juicy, sweet subacid.
wyken-pippin.note: Heading OCR'd 'Wykjen Pippin'; syn. Warwickshire Pippin, Girkin Pippin, Arley; after Ronalds.

yates.heading: Yates
yates.flavour: Flesh white, sometimes stained next the skin, tender, juicy, pleasant subacid.
yates.storage: great bearer and good keeper. ... March to May.

yellow-bellflower.heading: Yellow Bellflower
yellow-bellflower.flavour: Flesh tender, juicy, crisp, with a sprightly subacid flavor; before fully ripe it is considerably acid.
yellow-bellflower.quality: Very good. ... a large, handsome, and excellent winter Apple, everywhere highly esteemed in the United States.
yellow-bellflower.climate: it thrives well in the sandy soils of New Jersey.
yellow-bellflower.note: Syn. Bellefleur Yellow, Belle Fleur, Reinette Musque, Warren Pippin.

yellow-ingestrie.heading: Yellow Ingestrie
yellow-ingestrie.flavour: Flesh tender and delicate, with a plentiful juice when freshly gathered from the tree.
yellow-ingestrie.note: Downing keeps Summer Golden Pippin (line 23357) as a separate entry.

york-imperial.heading: York Imperial
york-imperial.flavour: Flesh yellowish, firm, crisp, juicy, pleasant, mild subacid.

hyslop.heading: Hyslop
hyslop.flavour: Flesh yellowish, subacid, good for culinary uses and for cider.
hyslop.quality: good for culinary uses and for cider.

transcendent.heading: Transcendent
transcendent.flavour: Flesh creamy yellow, crisp, subacid, a little astringent until fully mellow, when it is pleasant and agreeable.
transcendent.quality: This is one of the best of early autumn varieties.

siberian-crab.heading: Red Siberian Crab
siberian-crab.storage: Fit for preserving in September and October.
siberian-crab.note: The common Siberian Crab (Pyrus baccata) is introduced at line 26475 ('highly esteemed for preserving'); this entry describes only the small scarlet fruit.
